title: A step toward: Order 3 plane: no circuit of at most 64 AND/OR gates of fan-in two (distinct earlier wires) computes incidence and has a double re-read incidence
statement: ∀ (x1 : SimpleGraph (Fin (26 : ℕ))) [x2 : DecidableRel x1.Adj] (x3 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ (x4 x5 : Fin (26 : ℕ)), x1.Adj x4 x5 ↔ ∃ (x6 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) (x7 : Fin (13 : ℕ)), (x6 = x7 ∨ x6 = x7 + (1 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) ∨ x6 = x7 + (3 : Fin (13 : ℕ)) ∨ x6 = x7 + (9 : Fin (13 : ℕ))) ∧ (x4 = Fin.castAdd (13 : ℕ) x6 ∧ x5 = Fin.natAdd (13 : ℕ) x7 ∨ x5 = Fin.castAdd (13 : ℕ) x6 ∧ x4 = Fin.natAdd (13 : ℕ) x7)) → PEqualNP.TopForm.IsLeastAO x1 x3 → PEqualNP.TopForm.junk x1 x3 = ∅
unlocks: With its 2 sibling(s) it proves a posted step.
context: A hypothesis of a checked reduction, as Lean printed it.
sketch: Step 2 of 3 of a checked cut of L-meta-1482. Its sibling steps: L-meta-2389, L-meta-2393. Together they give the parent; the parent's own sketch: The exact least size at the plane of order 3: the star circuit has 64 gates. This side: no circuit of at most the stated size. SIZE, corrected 24 Nov: NOT a session-sized search by plain SAT; in-house controls show about eight times more time per gate (a 10-input case: 9 gates in 162 seconds, 12 gates unanswered in 3 minutes). Take it only with a real method: symmetry, a structural argument, or a construction for the side asking for a circuit. A circ
